hue: Lavender-purple to soft mauve-pink flowers above fresh green foliage
visual: Compact, upright, clump-forming perennial with aromatic green leaves and dense whorled flower heads made up of slender tubular lavender-purple flowers, creating a shaggy crown-like appearance.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth, especially during warm or dry weather. Water container plants regularly but ensure excess water drains freely.
aspect: Full sun to light partial shade. Best flowering and strongest compact growth occur in good light.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Do not allow to dry out badly in summer, as drought stress can encourage powdery mildew. Avoid excessive winter wet and waterlogged soil.
prune: Deadhead spent flowers to encourage further blooming, then cut stems down to ground level in autumn or leave seed heads for winter structure before cutting back in late winter.
cvs: BeeMine Lavender ('Balbeemav'); compact BeeMine Series cultivar bred for early flowering and strong resistance to powdery mildew.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most parts of the UK, tolerating approximately -15 to -10°C when established in suitably drained soil.
resilience: Notably resistant to powdery mildew compared with many older Monarda cultivars. Hardy, pollinator-friendly and generally robust, though young shoots may be damaged by slugs.
uses: Herbaceous borders, cottage gardens, prairie planting, wildlife and pollinator gardens, cut flowers and patio containers.
foliage: Deciduous, aromatic, ovate green leaves carried on upright square stems; forms a compact herbaceous clump.
container: Very good due to its compact habit; use a moisture-retentive but freely draining compost and avoid allowing the pot to dry out completely.
